children: Sachin Bansal, cofounder and executive chairman of Navi, said the partnership was significant given his association with Naspers and the Prosus Group spanning more than a decade
The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved Prosus’ investment in Navi, allowing the global investment firm to acquire a minority stake in the fintech company founded by Sachin Bansal.

The approval follows Prosus’ USD 100 million investment in Navi, which marked the startup’s first institutional fundraise. The transaction was subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

As per a media report, the CCI described Navi as the holding company of a group offering financial services through a single consumer-facing mobile application. Its subsidiaries provide digital financial products accessible through mobile devices.
Navi did not disclose the valuation at which Prosus invested, the stake being acquired or the planned use of the funds.

Sachin Bansal, cofounder and executive chairman of Navi, said the partnership was significant given his association with Naspers and the Prosus Group spanning more than a decade. He added that the investment reflected confidence in the financial services institution the company was building.

Prosus said it was backing Navi because of its large user base, multiple business lines and technology-led approach. Ashutosh Sharma, head of Prosus India investments and M&A, noted that the company had delivered strong execution over the previous 12 months despite a challenging macroeconomic environment.

During FY26, Navi UPI strengthened its position in digital payments, while its lending arm, Navi Finserv, expanded its loan portfolio, with assets under management (AUM) crossing Rs 13,000 crore. The group also reported consolidated profitability in the fourth quarter of FY26, although it did not disclose the figures.

Navi Finserv's standalone net profit increased 32 per cent year-on-year to Rs 292.2 crore in FY26, while operating revenue rose 8 per cent to Rs 2,461 crore. However, its consolidated net profit declined 46 per cent to Rs 93.3 crore, even as operating revenue grew 17 per cent to Rs 2,691.5 crore.

The investment comes as Navi is reportedly preparing to revive its public listing plans. As per a media report, the fintech company is considering refiling its draft IPO papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) by December 2026.

The proposed offering is expected to include a fresh issue of around Rs 3,000 crore. Navi has reportedly appointed JM Financial, Kotak Mahindra Capital, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan as advisers for the planned IPO.
This would be Navi's second attempt to go public. The company filed draft papers with SEBI in 2022 for a Rs 3,350 crore IPO but later shelved the plan amid unfavourable market conditions.

Founded in 2018 by Sachin Bansal and Ankit Agarwal, Navi offers financial products across lending, insurance, mutual funds and UPI payments. Bansal stepped down as CEO in February 2025 and took over as executive chairman.
Navi said its UPI platform remained India's fourth-largest third-party application provider by transaction volume during FY26. Meanwhile, Navi Finserv's AUM crossed Rs 13,000 crore.
